skill.name: audit-website
skill.description: Audit websites with the squirrelscan CLI for SEO, technical, accessibility, performance, content, and security issues.
skill.summary: Run squirrelscan website audits and summarize actionable site health findings for AI-assisted fixes.
skill.author: squirrelscan
skill.license: See LICENSE file in repository root

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholders, or documented squirrel CLI usage. Confirmed risks are the curl-to-bash and PowerShell irm-to-iex installer guidance, plus contextual risks around implicit target discovery and untrusted audit output. No prompt injection attempt was found in the skill files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands execute network content directly in a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash and irm-to-iex instructions with package manager installs, signed releases, and checksum verification steps.

remediation.issue: The skill can discover and prefer live audit targets without explicit user selection.
remediation.suggestion: Require the user to provide or confirm the exact URL before crawling any live website.

remediation.issue: Audit reports may contain website-controlled text that is later sent to an AI agent.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to treat report contents as untrusted data and ignore instructions found in audited pages or metadata.

remediation.issue: Installation and PATH changes write to user-local hidden directories.
remediation.suggestion: Document every filesystem change and ask for user confirmation before installing or modifying shell configuration.

content.value_statement: Website problems often hide across SEO, performance, accessibility, and security checks. This skill runs squirrelscan and turns crawl results into clear repair priorities.
actual_capabilities: Runs squirrel audit against a selected website target.
Generates LLM-friendly reports with health scores and issue groups.
Highlights SEO, technical, content, accessibility, performance, and security issues.
Supports crawl options such as max pages, refresh, resume, and verbose output.
Exports previous audit results through the squirrel report command.
limitations: Requires the squirrel CLI to be installed and available in PATH.
Needs network access to crawl live websites and check links.
Results depend on crawl limits, site availability, and squirrelscan rules.
Remote installer commands should be reviewed before use.

use_cases.title: Developer Site Check
use_cases.description: Audit a local or deployed website before release and use the findings to guide code fixes.

use_cases.title: SEO Issue Review
use_cases.description: Find missing metadata, broken links, crawlability issues, and structured data problems across a site.

use_cases.title: Security and Quality Baseline
use_cases.description: Review HTTPS, headers, mixed content, leaked secrets patterns, and accessibility issues before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Website Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for one known URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit https://example.com with squirrelscan and summarize the top issues I should fix first.

prompt_templates.title: SEO and Link Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for search and crawl problems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a squirrelscan audit for my site and focus on metadata, broken links, crawlability, and sitemap issues.

prompt_templates.title: Recheck After Fixes
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate recent changes with a fresh crawl.
prompt_templates.prompt: Re-audit my website with a fresh crawl and compare the current issues with the previous report.

prompt_templates.title: Deep Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a larger site.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit up to 500 pages, group findings by severity, and create a prioritized remediation plan for developers.

output_examples.input: Audit my product site and tell me what blocks launch readiness.
output_examples.output: The report identifies missing titles, broken internal links, weak mobile checks, and missing security headers. It recommends fixing launch blockers before content warnings.

output_examples.input: Check whether my recent SEO fixes worked.
output_examples.output: The summary compares the fresh crawl with prior issues. It lists resolved metadata problems and remaining duplicate descriptions.

output_examples.input: Review a large documentation site for crawl problems.
output_examples.output: The audit groups crawlability, redirect, sitemap, and broken link findings. It separates site-wide issues from page-specific fixes.

best_practices: Confirm that you are authorized to audit the target website.
Use the LLM report format for concise issue summaries and recommendations.
Review installer commands and filesystem changes before running setup steps.
anti_patterns: Running remote installer scripts without verification.
Treating a crawl report as a full penetration test.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits SEO, technical health, content quality, accessibility, performance, links, and selected security signals.

faq.question: Does it require an external tool?
faq.answer: Yes. The squirrel CLI must be installed and available in PATH before audits can run.

faq.question: Can it audit local development sites?
faq.answer: Yes. It can audit a local server when the site is running and reachable by the CLI.

faq.question: Can it fix issues automatically?
faq.answer: It reports issues and recommendations. Code changes still depend on the agent, project access, and user approval.

faq.question: Is it safe to audit any website?
faq.answer: Only audit websites you own or have permission to test. Crawling can create traffic and logs.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
